questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses, despite being at the MA level, were taught at a BA or even lower level of abstraction. There was a noticeable lack of depth, and the academic rigor did not meet the expected standards for a master’s program.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at the host institution was less engaging than at UCPH. Professors were unenthusiastic and not very responsive to questions, making it difficult to get clear explanations. Additionally, unlike UCPH, there were no supporting classes for assignments or discussions, limiting opportunities for feedback and academic growth.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The exams are very different from UCPH, they're mostly done in hand and only reviewed by the professor
Concentrate your visits from friends to few weekends, as is the easiest time to do something with the other Erasmus students

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk with other local students about the exams, how they are and how the evaluation is done. This is very useful for choosing the right courses.
